ev.waf_m_baobab.text: You were sent to gather baobab leaves for the sauce. You climbed higher than anyone and sat a long time in the branches, looking down at the village roofs.
ev.waf_m_pounding.text: Before dawn you and the neighbor women pound millet in the mortars. The pestles beat in time, someone starts a song, and the work goes easier.
ev.waf_m_griot_song.text: At a feast the griot sang about your lineage. He named your forebears one by one and told where they fought and what they built. You hadn't known so many names lived in you.
ev.waf_m_harmattan.text: The harmattan began to blow, the dry wind out of the desert. The sky turned yellow-grey, dust grits between your teeth, your lips crack, and the sun looks like a copper plate.
ev.waf_m_first_rain.text: The first rain came. The earth breathed, the air smelled of wet dust, and the whole village, old and young, rushed to sow while the soil was soft.
ev.waf_m_river_rise.text: The Niger is rising. Each morning the water is closer to the houses, canoes glide across the floodplain, and where goats grazed yesterday people are already fishing.
ev.waf_m_kola.text: An old man split a kola nut and handed you half. Bitter, mouth-puckering, but you can't refuse: kola is the sign of friendship and respect.
ev.waf_m_quran_board.text: You finally learned the sura written on your wooden board. The teacher told you to wash the ink off with water and drink it, so the words would stay inside you.
ev.waf_m_replaster.text: After the rains the whole town turned out to replaster the mosque with fresh mud. Some mix it, some carry baskets, others climb the wooden beams up the walls. Noise, laughter, mud to the elbows.
ev.waf_m_azalai.text: A salt caravan entered the town: hundreds of camels, each carrying two slabs of desert salt. The camels bellow, drivers in blue veils shout, and in the market everything except salt suddenly costs more.
ev.waf_m_salt_slab.text: In the market a trader sawed a slab of salt into pieces. Here a block like that buys a pinch of gold: salt from the north is worth every bit as much.
ev.waf_m_forge.text: You crept up to the forge. Goatskin bellows breathe like living things, sparks fly everywhere. The smith glanced at you and you ran: they say smiths have a power of their own.
ev.waf_m_komo_night.text: At night the Komo passed through the village: a terrible voice, drums. Women and children may not look on it. You lay under your blanket and listened, holding your breath.
ev.waf_m_hippo.text: At sunset a hippo's head rose from the water right beside the canoe. The boatman shouted and slapped the river with his paddle. It passed off, but your heart kept pounding for a long time.
ev.waf_m_fishing_pool.text: The water drew back and left fish trapped in the pools. At the master fisherman's signal the whole district waded in at once with nets and baskets. By evening there was fish for every family.
ev.waf_m_eid.text: The month of fasting is over. Everyone is in new clothes, the streets smell of roast meat and spices, the rich hand out alms, and children run from house to house for treats.
ev.waf_m_tabaski.text: For the Feast of Sacrifice a ram was slaughtered. The meat was split three ways: for the household, for kin and for the poor. A neighbor's boy ran off with his share, beaming.
ev.waf_m_market_tongues.text: In one morning at the market you heard five languages: Mandinka, Songhai, Fulfulde, Bozo and Arabic. The salt trader knew a little of each, and short-changed everyone equally.
ev.waf_m_fulani_milk.text: Fulani herders drove their cattle up to the village. Their women trade sour milk and butter for millet. You drank a whole calabash of it, thick and cool.
ev.waf_m_shea.text: You and the other women spend the whole day making shea butter: cracking the nuts, roasting, churning. The smoke stings your eyes and your hands shine with oil, but there's enough for cooking, for skin and for sale.
ev.waf_m_indigo.text: You dipped the cloth into the indigo vat a seventh time. It comes out green and turns blue before your eyes in the air. Your hands stay blue for a week: the mark of a dyer.
ev.waf_m_naming.text: On the seventh day the baby's head was shaved, and an elder whispered the name into its ear: {npc}. Then the name was announced aloud, the griot sang, and the guests were handed porridge and kola nuts.
ev.waf_m_copyists.text: In a scholar's house copyists bend over sheets of imported paper. They say books in Timbuktu sell for more than any other goods. You watched the lines run from right to left.
ev.waf_m_desert_stars.text: A night in the desert. The Tuareg guide showed you the stars the caravan steers by and said the sand remembers everyone who ever lost the way.
ev.waf_m_termites.text: After the rain winged termites poured out of the mound. The children caught hundreds of them and roasted them in a pan. Crunchy, with a nutty smell.
ev.waf_m_hare_tales.text: By the fire an old woman told how clever Hare tricked greedy Hyena yet again. Everyone roared, and afterwards you lay awake a long time working out how you would trick Hyena yourself.
ev.waf_m_wrestling.text: After the harvest, wrestling. Girls sing and clap, drums thunder. You pinned a youth from the next village and strutted for half the evening.
ev.waf_m_horseman.text: A noble horseman rode down the street. A horse from across the desert in an embroidered cloth, golden plates on its bridle, servants running behind. People step aside and lower their eyes.
ev.waf_m_dust.text: At the mansa's audience everyone who addressed the ruler poured dust on their own head. The mansa did not speak himself but through his griot, and everyone hung on every word.
ev.waf_m_cowries.text: You were taught to count cowries: by fives, then by twenties, then by hundreds. The shells come from somewhere beyond the sea, and nobody at the market knows where.
ev.waf_m_elder_tree.text: You sit with the elders in the shade of the council tree. Young people dip a knee to greet you as they pass, and quarrelling neighbors come to have you settle things.
ev.waf_m_locust_snack.text: A small swarm of locusts passed over the field. The adults cursed and waved branches, while the children caught them in calabashes: they'll be roasted tonight.
ev.waf_m_dates.text: A caravan trader gave you a handful of dates from a distant oasis. You made them last all day, one at a time.
ev.waf_m_rice.text: The water drained from the fields and you spent the day planting rice knee-deep in silt. The local rice is reddish and hardy, and grows where the Niger floods every year.
ev.waf_m_wedding_drums.text: All night the drums thundered next door: a wedding. Women sang, griots praised the groom's lineage and hinted at gifts. Sleep was impossible, and nobody tried.
ev.waf_m_well.text: At dawn you haul water from the deep well. The rope cuts your palms, and at the well, as always, there's all the news: who gave birth, who left, whose goat ran off.
ev.waf_d_initiation.title: Initiation
ev.waf_d_initiation.text: The boys of your age are led into the bush, to the initiation camp. Circumcision awaits them, weeks of trials, songs, secret words and the old men's stories. You will come back no longer children but one age-set, for life.
ev.waf_d_initiation.endure: Bear it in silence, like a man
ev.waf_d_initiation.endure.ok: You didn't make a sound. The boys of your age-set are now closer to you than kin.
ev.waf_d_initiation.ask: Listen to the old men and remember
ev.waf_d_komo.title: The Komo society
ev.waf_d_komo.text: The senior smith, keeper of the Komo mask, has invited you to join the society. Komo judges sorcerers, guards the village from evil and keeps knowledge of herbs and spirits. Whoever joins is bound by oath forever.
ev.waf_d_komo_later.title: The Komo council
ev.waf_d_komo_later.text: You are now one of the Komo elders. A woman has been brought before the society; her neighbors blame her for the deaths of children. The old men wait to hear what you will say.
ev.waf_d_komo_later.judge: Demand a cleansing rite and a fine
ev.waf_d_komo_later.mercy: Say the children died of fever, not sorcery
ev.waf_d_caste_love.title: The wrong caste
ev.waf_d_caste_love.text: You have fallen in love with someone of another caste: one of you from a free horon lineage, the other from the smiths. By custom such marriages cannot happen; the elders say mixing castes brings misfortune.
ev.waf_d_caste_love.insist: Try to win over the elders
ev.waf_d_caste_love.insist.success: The elders argued for a long time, a griot recalled an old precedent, and the marriage was allowed after all. People still whisper.
ev.waf_d_caste_love.insist.failure: You were refused, and word of your stubbornness spread through the district.
ev.waf_d_caste_love.elope: Run away together to another town
ev.waf_d_bridewealth.title: The suit
ev.waf_d_bridewealth.text: You have found a bride, and her kin are ready to talk. First kola nuts are sent, then cloth, livestock and cowries. If you lack that much, you can work some years in your future father-in-law's fields instead.
ev.waf_d_bridewealth.serve: Work it off in her family's fields
ev.waf_d_second_wife.title: A second wife
ev.waf_d_second_wife.text: Friends say a man of your standing should have more than one wife: more hands in the household, more children, more respect. {npc} says nothing but hears everything.
ev.waf_d_cowives_later.title: Co-wives quarrel
ev.waf_d_cowives_later.text: There's strife at home: your wives argue over whose turn it is to cook, whose children got the best pieces, and which of them you gave new cloth. The whole street can hear.
ev.waf_d_cowives_later.elder: Make the senior wife mistress of the house
ev.waf_d_quran_school.title: The marabout's school
ev.waf_d_quran_school.text: {npc} is growing up. The marabout on the next street teaches children the Quran and writing: wooden boards and ink at dawn, then begging for alms and work in his field by day. You pay a little, but always.
ev.waf_d_tribute.title: Tribute for the ruler
ev.waf_d_tribute.text: The village head has announced that each family must give a share of the harvest for the ruler: grain, honey, cotton. The court's envoys are already waiting.
ev.waf_d_tribute.hide.failure: They found the hiding place. You had to give double and hear a lot of hard words.
ev.waf_d_tribute.gift: Give the court's envoy a gift
ev.waf_d_pawn.title: Pawned
ev.waf_d_pawn.text: Your creditor has come for the debt. There is no money. He offers the usual way out: you will work off the debt in his house and fields until it is paid. It isn't slavery, but it isn't freedom either.
ev.waf_d_pawn.flee: Slip away by night to another town
ev.waf_d_griot_praise.title: A song in your honor
ev.waf_d_griot_praise.text: In the middle of the market a griot suddenly began to sing about you: your ancestors, your generosity, your wisdom. A crowd gathers. Everyone knows a song like that calls for a generous gift.
ev.waf_d_griot_mock.title: A mocking song
ev.waf_d_griot_mock.text: That griot you once slighted has made a song about you, funny and cruel. They sing it at weddings, and children shout the refrain after you in the street.
ev.waf_d_griot_mock.pay: Make peace with the griot and pay
ev.waf_d_griot_mock.laugh.success: You joined in the refrain yourself, and people stopped laughing at you and laughed with you instead.
ev.waf_d_griot_mock.laugh.failure: Your laugh rang false. They sing the song even louder.
ev.waf_d_hajj.title: The hajj
ev.waf_d_hajj.text: A pilgrim caravan is gathering for Mecca: across the desert, through Egypt and over the Red Sea. The road will take more than a year, and many never return. But whoever comes back will be called al-hajj for the rest of their life.
ev.waf_d_hajj.go.success: You endured the desert and the heat. Ahead lie Cairo, Mecca and the road home.
ev.waf_d_hajj.go.failure: On the way you fell gravely ill, but stubbornly kept going.
ev.waf_d_hajj_return.title: Al-hajj
ev.waf_d_hajj_return.text: You are back! The whole street turns out to meet you, and now they call you al-hajj. You have seen Cairo and its markets, the Kaaba, and crowds from every corner of the world.
ev.waf_d_hajj_return.books: Study the books you brought back
ev.waf_d_hajj_return.tell: Tell of the journey late into the night
ev.waf_d_divination.title: Divining with cowries
ev.waf_d_divination.text: Before an important undertaking you went to a diviner. He threw a handful of cowries on the mat, studied a long time how the shells fell, and said: offer a white chicken and wait seven days.
ev.waf_d_amulet.title: An amulet
ev.waf_d_amulet.text: A marabout offers you an amulet: a verse of the Quran written on a slip of paper and sewn into a leather pouch. He says it guards against arrows, sickness and the evil eye. Muslims wear them, and so do those who pray to the ancestors.
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.title: Cattle in the field
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.text: In the night a Fulani herd wandered into your field and trampled half the millet. The herdsman spreads his hands: cows don't know boundaries.
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.demand: Demand compensation before the village head
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.demand.success: The village head awarded you two goats.
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.demand.failure: The village head ruled you should have fenced your field. You even had to feed the witnesses.
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.forgive: Forgive and come to terms for the future
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.fight: Drive the herders off with a stick
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.fight.success: The herders left and didn't come back.
ev.waf_d_fulani_cattle.fight.failure: There were three of them. You barely got away.
ev.waf_d_runaway.title: A runaway
ev.waf_d_runaway.text: At night a gaunt man knocked at your door. He has run from his master and is heading south, toward where his village used to be. He asks you to hide him until morning.
ev.waf_d_runaway.hide.success: At dawn he left. No one ever found out.
ev.waf_d_runaway.hide.failure: The man's master tracked him down and demanded compensation from you.
ev.waf_d_runaway.food: Give him food and show him the road
ev.waf_d_runaway.report: Report him to the village head
ev.waf_d_runaway_thanks.title: An old debt
ev.waf_d_runaway_thanks.text: On the road a stranger came up to you with gifts, and you recognized the runaway. He reached his own people, is free now and trades. "I promised I'd come back," he says.
ev.waf_d_runaway_thanks.decline: Say there's nothing to thank you for
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.title: Freedom
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.text: You have served in the house for years. Slaves born in the household are no longer sold, and they work their own plots in the evenings. The master hints he could free you, for a price or as a pious deed.
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.buy: Buy your freedom with your savings
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.convert: Embrace Islam: freeing a fellow believer is a pious deed
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.convert.success: The master kept his word and declared you free before witnesses.
ev.waf_d_buy_freedom.convert.failure: The master praised your faith. But he never spoke of freedom again.
ev.waf_d_ferry.title: The crossing
ev.waf_d_ferry.text: You need to get across, and the Niger is in flood. The Sorko boatmen want double fare. Nearby an old man with a leaky little canoe offers to take you for next to nothing.
ev.waf_d_ferry.cheap.success: The old man knew the river like the back of his hand.
ev.waf_d_ferry.cheap.failure: The canoe shipped water and capsized near the bank. You scrambled out, but some of your things went to the bottom.
ev.waf_d_ancestor_shrine.title: An offering to the spirit of the land
ev.waf_d_ancestor_shrine.text: Before sowing the elders collect a little from everyone: at the sacred tree they will make an offering to the spirit of the land and to the first ancestors who founded the village. Without it, they say, the rain won't come.
ev.waf_d_ancestor_shrine.join: Go to the tree with everyone
ev.waf_d_ancestor_shrine.give: Give your share but stay out of the rite
ev.waf_d_manuscript.title: The manuscript
ev.waf_d_manuscript.text: A bookseller has brought a manuscript from Fez: a commentary on the law in a fine hand on imported paper. It costs as much as a good horse. You could also borrow it to copy it yourself.
ev.waf_d_manuscript.copy: Copy it in your own hand
ev.waf_d_manuscript_later.title: A book in the house
ev.waf_d_manuscript_later.text: Scholars have heard of your manuscript. A qadi asks to borrow it for a year to have a copy made for his students. A merchant offers more for it than you ever paid.
ev.waf_d_hunters.title: The hunters' brotherhood
ev.waf_d_hunters.text: The donso hunters invite you into their brotherhood. An old hunter will be your master: he'll teach you to read tracks, know the herbs and not fear the bush at night. Sundiata himself, they say, was a hunter.
ev.waf_d_audience.title: The royal audience
ev.waf_d_audience.text: You have a land dispute that only the ruler can settle. On audience days he sits beneath a silk canopy, and people speak to him through his griot herald. A petitioner is expected to sprinkle dust on his head.
ev.waf_d_audience.humble: Go in person and plead humbly
ev.waf_d_audience.humble.success: The ruler nodded, the griot repeated his words: the dispute went your way, and with a gift besides.
ev.waf_d_audience.humble.failure: You stumbled over your words in your nerves and never finished. The case was put off.
ev.waf_d_audience.griot: Pay a griot to speak for you
ev.waf_d_audience.griot.success: The griot spoke so beautifully that the ruler smiled. The ruling went your way.
ev.waf_d_audience.griot.failure: The griot took the money, but your turn never came.
ev.waf_d_drought.title: Drought
ev.waf_d_drought.text: There has been no rain for months. The millet has withered on the stalk, the wells are dropping, and grain prices rise every week. The old people say it hasn't been this bad since they were young.
ev.waf_d_drought.store: Buy grain while you still can
ev.waf_d_drought.rainmaker.success: A week later it rained. Coincidence or not, part of the harvest was saved.
ev.waf_d_drought.rainmaker.failure: The rain never came. The dry season was a hungry one.
ev.waf_d_locusts.title: Locusts
ev.waf_d_locusts.text: A cloud rolled in from the east, but not a rain cloud: locusts. They settle on the fields, and in an hour the millet is bare stalks.
ev.waf_d_locusts.smoke: Light fires and drive them off with smoke
ev.waf_d_locusts.smoke.success: Smoke and shouting worked: part of the field survived.
ev.waf_d_locusts.smoke.failure: The locusts paid no attention to the smoke or to you.
ev.waf_d_locusts.eat: Catch and dry the locusts for food: better than nothing
ev.waf_d_flood.title: The great flood
ev.waf_d_flood.text: The Niger has risen higher than the old people can remember. The water is eating at the mud walls; houses sag and collapse. Neighbors haul baskets of earth to the dike.
ev.waf_d_flood.dike: Shore up the dike with the others
ev.waf_d_flood.dike.success: The dike held. Your quarter was saved.
ev.waf_d_flood.dike.failure: The dike broke in the night. You had to build your house again from mud.
ev.waf_d_flood.leave: Carry your things to high ground
ev.waf_mv_study.title: Study in Timbuktu
ev.waf_mv_study.text: Your teacher says it's time for you to go further: to Timbuktu, to the scholars of the Sankore mosque. They read law, grammar, theology, even the stars. Students live in their masters' houses and live on alms.
ev.waf_mv_capital.title: Called to the capital
ev.waf_mv_capital.text: A man from the court is recruiting craftsmen, merchants and scribes for the capital, {capital}. They promise commissions, patronage and a place near the ruler. But there are more eyes watching there too.
ev.waf_mv_djenne.title: Move to Djenne
ev.waf_mv_djenne.text: A merchant you know is calling you to Djenne: gold and kola nuts come there from the south, and salt from the north by river. Whoever stands in the middle grows rich.
ev.waf_mv_djenne_later.title: At home in Djenne
ev.waf_mv_djenne_later.text: Over these years you have found your place in Djenne: you know who is honest, who has the best gold and when the boats will come. Now you can expand the business, or simply put down roots.
ev.waf_mv_djenne_later.expand: Hire agents and expand the trade
ev.waf_mv_djenne_later.settle: Buy a house and live quietly
ev.waf_mv_gao.title: Gao calls
ev.waf_mv_gao.text: Under the askias Gao has boomed: the army, the court, the landing places, the markets. They say everyone needs hands there, from potters to boatmen, and pays in silver and cowries.
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.title: A contest of griots
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.text: Griots from many villages have gathered for a great feast. Whoever sings best gets the host's gifts, and fame for a year.
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.epic: Sing the whole epic of Sundiata
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.epic.success: You sang till dawn and no one left. The host took a bracelet off his arm and gave it to you.
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.epic.failure: Halfway through you slipped in the genealogy. The old men noticed.
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.new: Compose a new song about the host
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.new.success: The song caught on at once; now they sing it all over the district.
ev.waf_j_griot_contest.new.failure: The song came out clumsy. The host frowned.
ev.waf_j_griot_house.title: Griot to a noble house
ev.waf_j_griot_house.text: A noble family offers to make you its griot: keeping its genealogy, speaking for the head of the lineage, making peace and arranging marriages. You'll be fed and rewarded well, but the service is for life.
ev.waf_j_smith_secret.title: The secret of the furnace
ev.waf_j_smith_secret.text: The old master has decided to pass on what few know: how to build the smelting furnace, what words to speak during the smelt, and what offerings to make so the ore gives up its iron.
ev.waf_j_smith_secret.own: Learn only the craft, without the rites
ev.waf_j_smith_spears.title: An order for spears
ev.waf_j_smith_spears.text: A war leader wants hundreds of spear and arrow heads for a campaign. He pays well, but then the farmers will have no new hoes for sowing.
ev.waf_j_forge_head.title: Head of the workshop
ev.waf_j_forge_head.text: The old master of your lineage has grown frail. Everyone agrees that the workshop, the apprentices and the orders are now yours to run.
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.title: The road to Taghaza
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.text: It's time to go for salt to Taghaza: twenty days across the desert there and as many back. You can join a big caravan and pay the Tuareg guides, or go with a small party, faster and without tolls.
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.big.success: It was slow going, but everyone made it. The salt sold at a profit.
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.big.failure: The caravan was stuck at a dry well and camels died. You came back with half the load.
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.fast.success: You arrived first, when salt was dear. Double the takings.
ev.waf_j_salt_caravan.fast.failure: You were attacked in the desert. You came back without your load, barely alive.
ev.waf_j_trading_house.title: A trading house of your own
ev.waf_j_trading_house.text: An old Wangara merchant is retiring and selling his business: camels, two large boats, a warehouse and agents in Djenne and Timbuktu. You can buy it all, or take a share.
ev.waf_j_trading_house.partner.success: The business thrived: your share brings in more than you expected.
ev.waf_j_trading_house.partner.failure: Your partner turned out to be crooked. Relations are ruined.
ev.waf_j_mine_shaft.title: A deep shaft
ev.waf_j_mine_shaft.text: Your shaft has gone ten men's heights into the earth. Down there the sand turns rich and yellow, but the walls are crumbling. The elders say the spirit of the earth dislikes the greedy.
ev.waf_j_mine_shaft.deeper.success: You hauled up a basket of sand glittering with gold and got out before the collapse.
ev.waf_j_mine_shaft.deeper.failure: The wall caved in. They dug you out, but your strength will be slow to return.
ev.waf_j_mine_shaft.stop: Fill in the shaft and dig a new one
ev.waf_j_marabout_war.title: Amulets for an army
ev.waf_j_marabout_war.text: A war leader asks for a hundred amulets so enemy arrows won't touch his men. He promises to pay generously. You know your verses comfort, but arrows sometimes find their mark anyway.
ev.waf_j_marabout_war.honest: Say all is in God's hands, and pray for the army
ev.waf_j_marabout_students.title: Students
ev.waf_j_marabout_students.text: Word of you has spread: students come from other towns and sit at your door with their boards. You could open a large teaching circle, or settle down to write a commentary of your own.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.title: A child with fever
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.text: In the night they brought a boy burning with fever. His family has already been to the marabout and to the diviner. Now all their hope is in you.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.herbs: A bark decoction and cool washing
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.herbs.success: By morning the fever broke. The boy asked for food.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.herbs.failure: Nothing helped. They carried the child away and looked at you with reproach.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.spirits: Find which spirit is offended and make an offering
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.spirits.success: Two days later the boy recovered. Your fame spread through the district.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.spirits.failure: The offering didn't help. The family went to find another healer.
ev.waf_j_healer_fever.refer: Send them to the physician in town
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.title: A lion near the village
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.text: For nights now a lion has been killing cattle at the next village. The elders have come to the donso hunters with kola nuts and a request.
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.lead: Track the beast and face it
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.lead.success: You struck the lion with a poisoned arrow. The griots have already made a song.
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.lead.failure: The lion was quicker. They carried you back to the village on a litter.
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.trap.success: Three nights later the lion fell into the pit.
ev.waf_j_hunter_beast.trap.failure: Only a neighbor's goat fell in.
ev.waf_j_boat_cargo.title: A heavy cargo
ev.waf_j_boat_cargo.text: A merchant asks you to take twice the usual load: grain and salt to Timbuktu while the water is high. He pays generously. The canoe will ride almost to the gunwales.
ev.waf_j_boat_cargo.load.success: You arrived without trouble, and the merchant paid a bonus.
ev.waf_j_boat_cargo.load.failure: At the rapids the canoe was swamped. You had to throw part of the cargo overboard.
ev.waf_j_horse.title: A horse
ev.waf_j_horse.text: Your commander noticed you in battle and is willing to take you into the cavalry. But the horse, brought across the desert, and the gear are for you to find: a horse costs as much as several slaves.
ev.waf_j_horse.serve.success: After the victory you were given a horse from the spoils.
ev.waf_j_chancery.title: The chancery at Gao
ev.waf_j_chancery.text: The court at Gao needs literate men to keep the tribute accounts and write letters to governors and to the merchants of the Maghreb. You are offered a post as an official.
ev.waf_j_indigo_order.title: Blue veils
ev.waf_j_indigo_order.text: A Tuareg merchant orders thirty veils at once, dyed so deep the color stays on the skin. Months of work.
ev.waf_j_indigo_order.share: Share the order with the neighbor women
ev.waf_j_overseer.title: In charge of the village
ev.waf_j_overseer.text: The master offers to put you in charge of the slave village: assigning work, reporting on the harvest. Life will get easier, but people will look at you differently.
ev.waf_d_levy.title: The levy
ev.waf_d_levy.text: The ruler is raising an army. Every village must send warriors with bows and spears, and the village heads are already drawing up lists. They say the campaign will be long, but the spoils rich.
ev.waf_d_levy.pay: Buy your way out with grain and a goat
ev.waf_d_levy.hide: Disappear into the bush for a while
ev.waf_d_levy.hide.failure: They found you and marched you to the camp while the whole village laughed.
ev.waf_j_become_marabout.title: A circle of pupils
ev.waf_j_become_marabout.text: You know the Quran by heart and read books better than most. Neighbors ask you to teach their children, and the old marabout is ready to give you an ijaza, a license to teach in his name.
ev.waf_d_healer_call.title: The spirits call
ev.waf_d_healer_call.text: After a long illness you began to dream the same dreams: herbs, a path into the bush, voices. The old healer says the spirits have chosen you, and the sickness won't leave until you study with her.
ev.waf_d_join_azalai.title: A driver in the caravan
ev.waf_d_join_azalai.text: The owner of a salt caravan is looking for young camel drivers. The pay is poor, but you can carry a little goods of your own, and in a few years lead a caravan yourself.
ev.waf_t_raid.title: The raid
ev.waf_t_raid.text: Horsemen fell on the village in the night. Roofs are burning, people screaming: the raiders are driving off the cattle and seizing people to sell in the northern markets.
ev.waf_t_raid.hide: Hide in the thickets by the river
ev.waf_t_raid.hide.success: You lay in the reeds until dawn. The raiders left, taking almost everything.
ev.waf_t_raid.hide.failure: They found you, bound you and led you north with the others.
ev.waf_t_raid.fight: Grab a spear and defend your home
ev.waf_t_raid.fight.success: You drove them off. The raiders left empty-handed, and people speak of you as a hero.
ev.waf_t_raid.fight.failure: You were wounded and taken away with the captives.
ev.waf_t_raid.flee: Run with what you can carry
ev.waf_t_nugget.title: The nugget
ev.waf_t_nugget.text: In the washing calabash something glinted that wasn't dust: a nugget the size of a nut. By law nuggets belong to the mansa; the people keep only the gold dust.
ev.waf_t_nugget.note: Fourteenth-century Arabic writers (al-Umari, Ibn Battuta) reported that in Mali nuggets belonged to the ruler while the people kept the gold dust. Gold was mined in Bambuk and Bure and sold to Wangara merchants.
ev.waf_t_nugget.give: Hand it to the village head for the mansa
ev.waf_t_nugget.sell: Sell it secretly to a merchant
ev.waf_t_nugget.sell.success: The merchant counted out cowries in silence and left that same night. You are rich.
ev.waf_t_nugget.sell.failure: The merchant informed on you. You were beaten and everything you owned was taken.
ev.waf_t_nugget.keep: Hide it as a family treasure
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.title: The well is dry
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.text: The well you marched six days to reach is choked with sand. The guide is sick and the water skins are almost empty. The next well is four days away, if you don't lose the way.
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.camels: Trust the camels: they can smell water
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.camels.success: On the second day the camels veered off and led you to a small well. The caravan is saved.
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.camels.failure: You wandered for days. Not everyone survived, and the cargo was abandoned in the sand.
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.drop: Drop part of the cargo and travel light
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.pray: Pray and wait for a passing caravan
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.pray.success: On the third day the camels of another caravan appeared on the horizon.
ev.waf_t_lost_caravan.pray.failure: Help came too late for many.
ev.waf_t_witch.title: Accused of sorcery
ev.waf_t_witch.text: Two children died in the village, then cattle. Someone remembered you had quarreled with their family. Now neighbors look away, and the elders speak of an ordeal.
ev.waf_t_witch.ordeal: Undergo the ordeal to prove your innocence
ev.waf_t_witch.ordeal.success: You came through the ordeal. The elders declared you innocent, and your accusers brought gifts.
ev.waf_t_witch.ordeal.failure: The ordeal was judged failed. You weren't driven out, but almost no one will speak to you.
ev.waf_t_witch.protector: Ask the marabout and the village head for protection
ev.waf_t_witch.protector.success: The marabout recited prayers, the village head forbade the talk. It all died down.
ev.waf_t_witch.protector.failure: They took your gifts, but the whispering behind your back didn't stop.
ev.waf_t_noble_notice.title: Saved from the river
ev.waf_t_noble_notice.text: A nobleman's canoe capsized near the bank, and you pulled his son out of the water. The next day a servant came: his master wishes to reward you.
ev.waf_t_noble_notice.serve: Ask to be taken into service at court
ev.waf_t_noble_notice.humble: Say anyone would have done the same
ev.waf_t_inheritance.title: The lineage's inheritance
ev.waf_t_inheritance.text: The head of the lineage has died. By old custom his authority and goods pass to the next brother; by Islamic law they are divided among the children in fixed shares. {npc} insists on deciding it their own way.
ev.waf_t_inheritance.qadi: Go to the qadi, the sharia judge
ev.waf_t_inheritance.qadi.success: The qadi decided the case by the book, and you received a good share.
ev.waf_t_inheritance.qadi.failure: The qadi got lost in the testimony, and the costs ate up a good deal.
ev.waf_t_inheritance.elders: Settle it by custom before the council of elders
ev.waf_t_inheritance.yield: Give way for the sake of peace in the family
ev.waf_t_flood_house.title: The house washed away
ev.waf_t_flood_house.text: In the night the sodden wall of your house collapsed, and the roof came down after it. In the morning there is a heap of mud where your house stood, and you dig through it for pots and mats.
ev.waf_t_flood_house.rebuild: Build the house again from mud
ev.waf_t_flood_house.kin: Move in with kin until you're on your feet
ev.waf_t_freed_will.title: The last will
ev.waf_t_freed_will.text: The master has died. His will was read before witnesses: following the custom of the pious, he frees some of his slaves, and you are among them. The heir scowls but dares not contest a dead man's will.
ev.waf_t_freed_will.leave: Leave and start a new life somewhere else
ev.waf_t_freed_will.stay: Stay nearby, free, under the family's protection
ev.waf_t_freed_will.serve: Stay and run the estate for the heir
ev.waf_t_coast.title: Strangers on the coast
ev.waf_t_coast.text: In the lower reaches of the Gambia river you saw huge boats with white sails. The Portuguese strangers have brought horses, cloth and brass basins. They take gold, but most of all they want to buy people.
ev.waf_t_coast.note: From the 1440s Portuguese ships traded on the Senegambian coast and later further south. In exchange for horses, cloth and metal they took gold and, increasingly, enslaved people: the beginnings of the Atlantic slave trade.
ev.waf_t_court_fall.title: Disgrace
ev.waf_t_court_fall.text: The courtier you served, to whom you owed everything, has fallen from favor: he is accused of plotting against the ruler. Now all his people are under suspicion.
ev.waf_t_court_fall.plead: Go to court and swear your loyalty
ev.waf_t_court_fall.plead.success: They believed you. A new patron took you under his wing.
ev.waf_t_court_fall.plead.failure: They didn't believe you. Half your property was seized for the treasury.
ev.waf_t_court_fall.flee: Get far away from the court
ev.waf_f_ramadan.title: Fasting in the heat
ev.waf_f_ramadan.text: Ramadan has fallen in the hottest season. Not a sip of water from dawn to dusk, and the work won't wait. The old marabout says the sick and travelers may postpone the fast.
ev.waf_f_ramadan.ease: Work less and keep the fast
ev.waf_f_ramadan.secret: Drink water secretly in the field
ev.waf_f_ramadan.secret.failure: A neighbor saw you with the calabash. By evening the whole street knew.
ev.waf_f_convert.title: The merchants' faith
ev.waf_f_convert.text: A merchant you have long done business with invites you to the mosque. He says Muslims get credit more easily, are welcome in any town from Djenne to Cairo, and that God is one and merciful.
ev.waf_f_convert.convert: Speak the shahada and embrace Islam
ev.waf_f_convert.both: Go to the mosque without forgetting the ancestors
ev.waf_f_convert.refuse: Stay true to the spirits of the ancestors
ev.waf_f_ancestors_call.title: The voice of the ancestors
ev.waf_f_ancestors_call.text: One misfortune after another. An aunt whispers that the ancestors are offended because you forgot them for the mosque. You must bring an offering to the lineage altar, as everyone before you did.
ev.waf_f_ancestors_call.both: Bring the offering and still pray at the mosque
ev.waf_f_ancestors_call.return: Return to the faith of the ancestors
ev.waf_f_ancestors_call.pray: Pray to God alone and ask the imam's advice
ev.waf_f_minority.title: A different faith
ev.waf_f_minority.text: Almost everyone around you follows another faith: {other_faith}. At festivals they expect you to join in, and they look askance when you pray your own way.
ev.waf_f_minority.blend: Go to the festivals but pray your own way
ev.waf_f_friday.title: Friday prayer
ev.waf_f_friday.text: On Friday the great mosque is full; the rows of worshippers spill into the street. After the sermon the poor, the blind and the marabouts' pupils wait at the gates with their bowls.
ev.waf_f_friday.small: Drop a couple of cowries in a bowl
ev.waf_f_holey.title: The spirit dance
ev.waf_f_holey.text: At night by the river they play the one-string fiddle and beat on calabashes. They say the spirits of the river and the ancestors come down into the dancers and speak through their mouths.
ev.waf_f_grove.title: The sacred grove
ev.waf_f_grove.text: Everyone needs new fields, and nearby stands the old grove where the spirits live and only the old people go. Some say it's time to clear it; others, that it will bring disaster on the whole village.
